config.description: CONTROL for the raggedness gate: chunked prefill DISABLED. With it on, a ragged batch paid only for its packed tokens and batch padding was rejected by 44-618%. Chunked prefill is what concatenates requests into one step, so it is the obvious cause. If batch padding reappears here, the finding is 'chunked prefill removes length padding' -- narrow, and directly comparable to LAPS and BucketServe, which do not use it. If cost stays packed, the finding is about the TPU serving path itself and is far more general.
config.note_budget: Batch-padded totals are allowed to exceed max_num_batched_tokens here, unlike the gate run: that constraint existed only to keep the batch-padding PREDICTION in-budget for a clean three-way test, and batch padding is now rejected. Under packed behaviour the step holds total_tokens regardless of spread, so nothing splits.
config.note_controlled: enable_chunked_prefill is deliberately FALSE here and True everywhere else. This is the one place a controlled variable is intentionally flipped, it is recorded in the config so the audit sees it, and no result from this run may be pooled with the chunked-prefill-on runs.
config.note_controls: The two max_len=512 cells are uniform, so all three models predict the same cost. They cannot distinguish anything and are not meant to: they check the MEASUREMENT. If a control disagrees with every model, the verdict on the ragged cells is untrustworthy.
config.note_separation: Predicted costs at n=4, total=2048, max=1536 are 39.2 / 56.6 / 144.8 ms for packed / per-request-padded / batch-padded -- a 3.7x spread, far outside the measurement noise, so the cell decides rather than hints.
config.note_spread: max_len is the only variable; n and total tokens are held exactly. The uniform cells (max_len=512) remain controls.
